claim: Visual context and layout understanding are crucial for effective document extraction; multi-modal LLMs effectively leverage this information when processing images directly, leading to higher accuracy compared to structured parsing that loses visual context.
falsifier: Compare extraction accuracy between direct image input and a pipeline that strips visual layout (e.g., plain text extraction) while controlling for model and prompt.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Availability of visual context–extraction accuracy mechanism

claim: Probabilistic verifier progress scores increase monotonically along successful agentic trajectories but remain largely flat on stalled or failing trajectories, allowing the same scalar to serve as both a progress measure and an early-warning signal.
falsifier: On sampled agentic trajectories labeled by outcome, compute rank correlation between step index and verifier progress score separately for successful and failed trajectories.

conditions: agentic coding trajectories from Terminal-Bench V2
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Trajectory outcome–verifier progress score as principle
